title: Oven Cavity Temperature Probe Failure
shortDescription: Cavity RTD or thermocouple is open, shorted, or reading out of range.
fullDescription:
Vulcan convection ovens (VC4, VC6, VC44, SG4) display F1 when the cavity temperature sensor reports an invalid reading. The burner or element is immediately locked out for safety because without a valid temperature reading the oven could runaway.

Most commonly caused by the probe tip being cracked from rack impact, wire damage from heat cycling at the bulkhead grommet, or a failed connection at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Power off and access back
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off gas/power, remove rear service panel to access probe harness.

fixSteps.title: Test probe
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect probe, measure resistance at room temp (RTD ~110 ohm, type-K thermocouple microvolts). Out of spec = replace.

fixSteps.title: Install new probe
fixSteps.instruction: Route through grommet, secure clip, connect to board, verify reading on startup.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — gas models require gas-licensed technicians.
videoSearchQuery: Vulcan VC4 F1 oven probe replace

faq.q: Will F1 clear with the oven cool?
faq.a: Only if the probe is intermittent; once the probe element is open, the code stays.

title: Ignition Failure
shortDescription: Gas ignitor failed to light the burner within the trial-for-ignition period.
fullDescription:
F2 on Vulcan gas convection ovens means the spark or hot-surface ignitor did not prove flame within the ignition controller's trial period (typically 4-10 seconds). The gas valve closes and lockout occurs, requiring a manual reset.

Causes range from no gas supply (turned off valve, empty LP tank) to a dirty flame sensor or failed ignitor module.

causes.cause: Gas supply valve off or LP empty

symptoms: Click from ignitor with no light

fixSteps.title: Confirm gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Check manual valve open and LP tank not empty. Cycle power to reset lockout.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Shut gas/power, remove flame rod, gently polish with fine abrasive pad, reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Test ignitor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure ignitor resistance cold; hot surface ignitor should be 40-200 ohm typical. Open = bad.

fixSteps.title: Call gas technician
fixSteps.instruction: If ignitor and sensor test OK but no flame, the gas valve or ignition module needs professional service.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — gas system work is code-regulated and unsafe without proper tools.
videoSearchQuery: Vulcan convection oven F2 ignition fault

faq.a: If you smell gas, shut off supply at the manual valve and ventilate — call a professional immediately.

title: Flame Loss During Operation
shortDescription: Flame was established but the sensor lost signal during the heating cycle.
fullDescription: F3 means the burner was burning normally but the flame rectification signal dropped below threshold. Causes include a dirty flame rod, inadequate gas pressure under load, or a drafty install that blows the flame off the sensor.

causes.cause: Exhaust hood pulling draft through oven

symptoms: F3 after several minutes of heating

fixSteps.title: Clean flame rod
fixSteps.instruction: Polish flame sensor as in F2; confirm ceramic insulator is not cracked.

fixSteps.title: Check manifold pressure
fixSteps.instruction: With burner running, measure manifold pressure per spec plate. Low pressure = gas service issue.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — gas pressure measurement is professional only.

faq.a: Yes — an oversized exhaust hood without makeup air can pull flame off the sensor.

title: Convection Blower Fault
shortDescription: Convection fan did not reach commanded RPM or motor overload tripped.
fullDescription: The convection blower is monitored by an RPM tach or by motor amp draw. F4 indicates the fan has stalled, is under-speed, or has tripped its overload. Without convection airflow the oven cavity will not heat evenly and the control inhibits the burner as a safety.

fixSteps.title: Listen / inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Power off completely, spin blower wheel by hand, check for play or rub.

fixSteps.title: Reset overload
fixSteps.instruction: Reset motor overload button at control panel and retest.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If bearings growl or wheel seized, replace motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — blower assembly requires cavity disassembly.

faq.q: Can I run in radiant mode?
faq.a: No — Vulcan convection ovens require the fan running to prevent element/burner over-temp.

title: High Limit Thermostat Tripped
shortDescription: Cavity high-limit safety has tripped — oven shutdown.
fullDescription:
F5 means the mechanical high-limit thermostat (typically 575-625F) opened and cut power/gas to the burner. Usually indicates the primary control failed to modulate or the convection fan stopped while heating.

This is a safety event — do not defeat the high limit.

causes.cause: Cavity probe drifted low causing overheat

fixSteps.title: Allow full cool-down
fixSteps.instruction: Let oven cool to room temp before investigating.

fixSteps.title: Reset manual high limit
fixSteps.instruction: Press high-limit reset button on rear of control enclosure.

fixSteps.title: Investigate root cause
fixSteps.instruction: If F5 returns, the root cause (fan, probe, gas valve) must be diagnosed.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — F5 indicates a safety event that must be fully diagnosed.
videoSearchQuery: Vulcan oven F5 high limit trip

faq.q: Why did the high limit trip?
faq.a: High limit is a last-resort safety — something else failed first. Do not just reset and continue.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: Door position switch inconsistent with expected state.
fullDescription: Vulcan ovens may use a door switch to pause the blower momentarily when doors open to prevent heat loss. F6 means the controller sees a mismatch — door shown closed but switch open, or vice versa.
symptoms: Blower does not slow at door open

fixSteps.title: Inspect actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Open door, verify actuator flag is straight and clean.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Test continuity with door open/closed; replace if inconsistent.

whenToCallPro: Usually DIY; pro if switch is inside the hinge tower.

faq.a: No — cycle still runs but blower modulation is disabled.

title: Controller Communication Fault
shortDescription: Display and main board have lost serial communication.
fullDescription: F7 indicates the HMI display cannot talk to the main control board over the internal bus. Usually a harness issue; occasionally a failed board.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle power at breaker, wait 2 minutes, restore.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Access HMI back, reseat communication ribbon.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.q: Can I run in manual mode?
faq.a: Generally no — HMI is required for setpoint input.

title: Slow Heating Fault
shortDescription: Oven is not reaching setpoint within the expected time.
fullDescription: F8 is logged when the cavity has failed to rise to setpoint within a programmed time. On electric ovens this usually means a failed element or contactor; on gas, low manifold pressure or a partly blocked burner.

fixSteps.title: Test elements / contactor
fixSteps.instruction: On electric, measure each element; on gas, check flame quality and manifold pressure.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — elements are 208/240V.
videoSearchQuery: Vulcan VC4 F8 slow heating element

faq.q: Can I use the oven with F8?
faq.a: Not reliably — food safety depends on actual cook temps.

title: Steam Injection Fault (Combi Models)
shortDescription: Steam injection system failed to produce steam on command.
fullDescription: On Vulcan combi-style ovens, F9 indicates the steam generator did not produce steam — either water supply problem, a clogged injector nozzle, or a failed steam solenoid.
symptoms: No steam at start of bake

fixSteps.title: Check water supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm supply valve open, inline filter clean.

fixSteps.title: Descale injector
fixSteps.instruction: Run descale cycle per manual or manually remove nozzle and soak.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — steam plumbing is pressurized.
videoSearchQuery: Vulcan SG steam injection F9 fault

faq.a: Yes — a softener/RO prefilter extends injector life significantly.

title: Salamander Broiler Over-Temp
shortDescription: Salamander cavity temperature exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription: Vulcan salamander broilers (VSB, VSALH) show FE when the upper radiant section over-temps. Often because the element was left on unattended, or the cavity probe failed low.

fixSteps.title: Allow cool-down
fixSteps.instruction: Let salamander cool fully before diagnosing.

fixSteps.title: Reset and test
fixSteps.instruction: Reset high-limit and operate with a thermometer check.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.q: Can a stuck contactor be welded shut?
faq.a: Yes — contactor contacts can weld closed, requiring replacement.
